document_meta.title: California's Forests and Rangelands: 2017 Assessment and 2020 Strategy Report
document_meta.document_type: Forest and Range Assessment / Strategy Report

orientation.summary: This document is a combined California state Forest and Range Assessment (2017) and associated Strategy Report (2020), produced by CAL FIRE (California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection). The document is highly climate-aware, treating climate change as a fundamental threat to forest and rangeland sustainability, wildfire regimes, carbon storage, water resources, and wildlife habitat. It discusses range shifts and vegetation type conversions driven by climate change, particularly for timberlands, oak woodlands, Joshua tree, and aspen habitats, using niche modeling outputs from GCMs (CNRM CM5 and MIROC ESM under RCP8.5) to project future habitat suitability. The assessment primarily synthesizes analyses performed by external researchers and state programs (e.g., Thorne et al. 2017), rather than conducting new modeling itself. Management actions addressing climate adaptation include reforestation using climate-appropriate seed sources, habitat connectivity, refugia identification, assisted migration (mentioned for seed zones), and conservation easements.

projects: King Fire ponderosa and sugar pine reforestation experiment: 12 sources of ponderosa and sugar pines are being evaluated under 'operational' conditions to determine if seed source influences growth, with source locations correlated with climatic variables. Provides evidence on climate-adaptive seed sourcing.

Sierra Nevada Adaptive Management Program (SNAMP): Measured water quality and quantity variables before and after treatment implementation. Found that non-commercial thinning has minimal hydrologic impacts, providing evidence for forest health treatment efficacy.
Vasco Wind Energy Center turbine replacement: Tripled energy production and achieved 70% reduction in avian mortality, providing case-study evidence for best practices in renewable energy impacts.

Effectiveness Monitoring Committee (EMC) under Board of Forestry: Ongoing program assessing the efficacy of Forest Practice Rules at protecting forest resources, providing iterative feedback to policymakers.
